text:
marina: heads-up: reproducing a steady GPU memory growth on H100 when streaming long contexts (~64k) across repeated evict+refill cycles. looks like the pagetable keeps accumulating "shadow" allocations even after entries are evicted. not sure if it's a bookkeeping leak or a timing window. :thinking:

devin: repro steps? which model / kernel path?

marina: small repro harness attached locally — run streaming test with batch=1, seq=64k, request rate ~1 req/s. observed growth over ~30m until OOM on 80GB. kernels: paged-attn path, hybrid-pager, kernel selection lands on fast-prefetch for first few passes then falls back to naive for refill.

ryan: can you paste the nvprof/CUPTI snippet where growth shows up?

marina: pasted, see timeline: heavy allocation spikes during page table rebuilds, then small lingering allocations tagged as "pt_shadow" in our debug allocator. here's a trimmed log: 

```
[08:12:11] alloc_pt_page id=0x7f9c65 size=4096 owner=stream-7
[08:12:11] map_entry idx=2345 -> page=0x7f9c65
[08:12:11] evict_entry idx=2345 tombstone=true
[08:12:11] release_page deferred->shadow_list.push(0x7f9c65)
...
[08:37:22] garbage_collect_shadow: scanned=0 reclaimed=0
[08:37:25] alloc_pt_page id=0x7f9c71 size=4096 owner=stream-9
```

marina: note the garbage_collect_shadow doesn't reclaim because owner_stamp mismatches after a migration (owner moved from stream-7 to stream-9). suspect stale owner stamp prevents reclamation.

sourabh: hmm, that sounds like a race between eviction handler and the compaction pass. when we remap pages during rapid refills, owner_stamp we compare is a 32-bit counter that can wrap/overwrite if the same stream id is reused. could be an ABA.

jia: did you see any different behavior on A100 vs H100?

marina: yes — A100 stable, H100 shows the growth. hypothesize due to different scheduling (H100 uses more fine-grained streams for prefetch kernels) so stream id reuse frequency increases. Also kernel selection on H100 triggers a different refill codepath that defers reclamation to a host thread which misses the window.

ryan: can you attach a pprof snippet of the shadow_list length over time? also capture pt_entry->owner_stamp values for a sample index.

marina: attaching short dump inline: shadow_list_len: [2,3,5,8,12,20,33] over 30m. sample owner_stamps for idx=2345: [0x110, 0x110, 0x114, 0x114, 0x118]. reclamation code expects monotonic increase but we saw non-monotonic after remap.

devin: quick mitigation: make garbage_collect_shadow treat owner_stamp mismatch as reclaimable if the page is unreferenced and has been on shadow_list > threshold_ms (say 60s). that'll reduce growth until proper fix.

ryan: agree as short-term. long-term we should avoid relying on stream id identity. options: 1) use a monotonically increasing global eviction epoch (64-bit) that increments on each eviction and compare epochs instead of stream ids, or 2) set a tombstone bit in the PT entry and have a safe reclamation epoch that doesn't rely on owner equality.

marina: i wrote a quick patch for option (1). small diff:

```
- if (entry->owner == owner_stamp) reclaim(page);
+ if (entry->evict_epoch <= local_epoch) reclaim(page);
+ // bump local_epoch on each successful eviction
```

marina: patched on my branch, ran the same streaming harness for 2h with no growth on H100.

sourabh: nice. any perf regressions from new checks?

marina: negligible — added a 64-bit compare in the hot path but the branch is almost always false except during gc. measured median token latency +0.2ms on H100, within noise.

jia: let's get an experimental canary on dedicated infra (rtx pool + h100) and run our regression suite (batching heuristics, kernel selection combos). also add a unit test that simulates stream id reuse and ensures reclamation.

devin: also worth adding logging hook to track shadow_list length and reclamation events so SRE can alert before OOM. add a metric: kvcache_shadow_count and kvcache_shadow_age_max.

ryan: assign to eng-runtime to turn patch into PR + add regression tests. mariana? (ccing devops)

marina: i'll open the PR today, include the canary yaml. tagging the patch with "evict-epoch-fix".

ci-bot: build queued for branch "marina/evict-epoch-fix" — ETA 12m. :gear: 

devin: once CI passes, canary to 'dedicated-h100-canary' for 24h. if shadow_count stays flat, we merge.

sourabh: follow-up: we should also audit other places that used owner_stamp comparisons (prefetch, reorder buffers). may be more latent ABA bugs.

marina: agreed. adding an issue to track owner_stamp -> epoch migration across modules. thanks all. :tada:
